newsitem.title: UK: Reuters says no change on buy-back stance.
newsitem.headline: Reuters says no change on buy-back stance.

text.p: International news and information group Reuters Holdings Plc denied on Monday it had taken a definitive decision to shelve plans to return surplus cash to shareholders.

The Observer newspaper on Sunday reported that a plan to return cash via a special share dividend, postponed in October, had now been put off completely because the company could not find a distribution method which treated all shareholders equally.
"Our position has not changed from when we responded to the October 8 Treasury statement," a Reuters spokesman said.
Reuters announced plans earlier this year to return 613 million stg via a share buy-back and special dividend issue and its shareholders were due to vote on the proposal on October 9.
However on October 8 the Treasury announced a tax amendment, abolishing tax credits for shareholders of companies offering share buy-back schemes or linked to special dividend payouts.
Consequently Reuters shareholders voted to delay consideration of the buy-back plans and bonus dividend issue.
The resolutions relating to this were postponed indefinitely as Reuters said it would be imprudent to proceed given the uncertainty created by the government's statement on the issue.
The company said at the time that it would continue to review available options for returning cash to sharholders.

Draft legislation on the taxation of share buy-back schemes and special dividend issues was published last week and will be included in the next Finance Bill, full details of which will be published in January.
"We will have to wait and see the details of the Finance Bill," the spokesman said.
"The Treasury knows our position. We would favour a move to the U.S. position of being able to buy and sell our own stock for treasury..(without adverse tax effects)," he said.
"The company still believes that cash which is surplus to requirements...should be returned to shareholders," he added.
